source_doubts.quote: so the conclusion follows from the companion unitarizability theorem \cite[Theorem~1.1]{OpenAIUnitarizability2026}. ... Apply the companion percolation result \cite[Corollary~1.2]{OpenAIPercolation2026} to \(F\)
source_doubts.problem: The proofs are pure citations to unpublished companion papers. What they would need is very strong: that every countable nonamenable group has a non-unitarizable uniformly bounded representation with norm at most 1+ε, which is a strong form of a negative answer to Dixmier's unitarizability problem (open as far as I know), and that p_c<p_{2→2}≤p_u, and hence p_c<p_u, holds on every Cayley graph of a nonamenable group, which includes the Benjamini–Schramm conjecture (open in general as far as I know). Nothing in the source verifies these statements, so the corollaries are conditional on the companion papers.

unverified_marks.concern: The two corollaries rest only on citations to companion papers that could not be checked. The general statements those papers would have to contain (every countable nonamenable group is non-unitarizable with norm at most 1+ε; p_c<p_{2→2}≤p_u and non-uniqueness on every nonamenable Cayley graph) are strong.
